core_memory.academic_progress: transitioning from intro to advanced topics like algorithmic concepts, system design, and quantum computing basics
core_memory.topics_covered: dynamic programming, approximation algorithms for NP-hard problems

archival_memory.course_distributed_systems: CS 2631, second hardest course, involves heavy reading, group discussions, and a major project simulating a decentralized file storage system
archival_memory.group_project_challenges: collaborating with peers having different coding styles and project ideas; handling concurrency issues and node failures
archival_memory.project_milestone: spending hours troubleshooting a bug caused by a misplaced bracket in a config file; achieving accomplishment after fixing the issue
archival_memory.elective_game_design: counts toward major when combined with specific classes; professor is industry veteran with experience in indie games; covers 2D/3D engines, physics implementation, and UX design
archival_memory.assignment_example: designed a labyrinth-based mini-game focusing on balancing difficulty curve to prevent player frustration; challenging but rewarding to develop
archival_memory.class_quantum_computing: Introduction to Quantum Computing; initially intimidating but now enjoyed; professor focuses on conceptual understanding with linear algebra and code examples in quantum circuit simulation frameworks; studying theoretical advantages of Grover's and Shor's algorithms over classical methods
archival_memory.capstone_project: end-of-year project using machine learning to analyze social media sentiment for emergency response; involves real-time detection of crisis indicators from tweets or posts; building an interface for city officials or campus security; integrates database management, API development, front-end design, and ML pipeline; includes project management with agile practices like sprints and daily stand-ups
archival_memory.elective_philosophy_of_mind: last required non-CS elective; explores consciousness, mind, and implications for AI; small class with focus on discussions; helps bridge technical knowledge with ethical considerations; wrote a paper on whether strong AI could ever experience qualia, such as subjective experiences of color or pain
archival_memory.class_schedule_mondays_wednesdays: 9:30 AM: Advanced Algorithms; short break; 11:00 AM: Distributed Systems lecture; after lunch: Capstone meetings(varied: lectures, lab work, team time)
archival_memory.class_schedule_tuesdays_thursdays: morning: Quantum Computing; afternoon: Game Design; Thursday evening: Philosophy of Mind
archival_memory.friday_schedule: no scheduled classes; spent on assignments, group projects, or labs; also engaged in undergrad research on data visualization for big scientific datasets
archival_memory.project_challenges: Capstone project consumes 10+ hours weekly, especially when encountering bugs or model training issues; Distributed Systems project also demands significant time; group meets at least twice a week; relies on Slack or Discord for coordination; scheduling five people is challenging but valuable for academic, hands-on learning without job pressures
archival_memory.overall_experience: transitioned from dreading tough CS classes to feeling confident in problem-solving and time management; occasional late nights due to debugging or deadlines; senior year has built confidence in resourcefulness, collaboration, and critical thinking; all coursework directly contributes to future career goals; finds the experience rewarding and personally fulfilling
archival_memory.hobby_sailing: Sailing is a unique hobby where the user grew up near a marina and was introduced to it by their dad. They now participate in a local student-friendly sailing club, enjoying the freedom and problem-solving aspects of navigating unpredictable wind and water conditions, which resonates with their problem-solving mindset in programming.
archival_memory.hobby_gym: The user started going to the gym in their freshman year of college, initially learning basic lifting routines from a dorm friend. They now exercise four times a week, focusing on incremental improvements in strength and energy levels. They view it as a vital stress-reliever and mental clarity booster, especially after long coding sessions, which enhances their productivity and sleep quality.
archival_memory.hobby_gaming: The user enjoys co-op survival and fast-paced shooter games, viewing them as strategic and collaborative experiences that provide mental challenges and social connection. As a CS major, they often play on PC and have dabbled in game development using Unity or Unreal Engine for fun, expressing interest in exploring this area more deeply in the future to bridge the gap between playing and creating games.
archival_memory.hobby_reading: The user has a long-standing passion for reading, particularly sci-fi and fantasy novels, which were introduced by their mother. Currently, they are deeply engaged with AI-themed sci-fi literature, such as 'The Infinity Courts' by Akemi Dawn Bowman, which connects to their academic interests in artificial intelligence. Reading serves not only as a form of relaxation but also as a way to explore ethical and social implications of technology, helping them reflect on philosophical questions related to their future work in computer science.
archival_memory.hobby_scheduling: The user schedules their hobbies systematically, similar to how they manage study time. Every Sunday, they plan activities based on weather and availability: gym sessions or lake trips on nice days, indoor co-op gaming or apartment workouts on rainy days, and a consistent 30-minute reading session before bedtime. This structured approach helps maintain a healthy balance between academic responsibilities and personal interests, promoting both physical well-being and mental relaxation.
archival_memory.hobby_combination_sailing_gaming: The user has combined sailing and gaming as hobbies, noting that both involve teamwork, coordination, and problem-solving. During a specific day, they sailed at the lake in the morning, then played co-op video games in the evening, drawing a parallel between managing sails and leading in-game strategy. This experience highlights how each hobby demands roles, attention to detail, and collaborative effort, reinforcing their appreciation for the shared problem-solving and teamwork elements across different activities.
archival_memory.hobby_persistence_strategy: The user acknowledges the stress of a packed academic and work schedule, dominated by lectures, labs, homework, research meetings, and tutoring. Despite this, they emphasize that passion for hobbies enables them to maintain engagement through small, manageable increments. For example, reading one chapter at a time, sailing once a month, or playing a quick game session in 30 minutes. This flexible, incremental approach allows them to sustain their hobbies even within tight time constraints, reflecting resilience and adaptability in balancing academic and personal life.
archival_memory.research_lab_focus: Data visualization for big scientific datasets
archival_memory.research_professor_feedback: Recognized ability to bridge technical coding with user experience
archival_memory.research_motivation: Transformative experience that aligned with interest in real-world problem-solving and data-driven insights
archival_memory.first_research_project: Visualized oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group using daily buoy data from the Pacific. Aggregated and presented patterns over months and years through data cleaning scripts, real-time update pipelines, and interactive interfaces. Co-authored first research paper; felt surreal and proud upon seeing name in publication.
archival_memory.campus_community_involvement: As a fourth-year Computer Science student, I’ve discovered various communities that make campus life vibrant and feel like a second home, with many opportunities to get involved beyond just coding. Joined the Computer Science Society during sophomore year; hosts weekly meetups on new technologies, project sharing, and industry speakers. A welcoming environment for beginners, providing peer support on topics like concurrency and containerization.
archival_memory.vr_ar_club_details: Attending VR/AR Club since sophomore year, focused on immersive analytics. Club has a hands-on VR lab with headsets, sensors, and prototypes. Hosts demos where members showcase projects like AR tutors for advanced math, providing 3D demonstrations of equations. The supportive and creative environment inspires further research in emerging technologies.
archival_memory.student_radio_station_events: Occasionally attends student-run radio station events, particularly open-mic nights where people perform singing, poetry, or stand-up comedy. Remembered a friend from the Distributed Systems class performing an acoustic set, showcasing a different side of personality that highlights the diversity of experiences beyond coding and group projects.
archival_memory.campus_central_lawn_events: The central lawn is a popular hangout spot between classes, with student organizations setting up booths to promote events like a cappella groups or environmental activism. Freebies like stickers or candy are offered to attract interest. Personal preference for free pizza makes clubs with pizza in their ads particularly appealing. The lawn hosts major events like Tech Fest, where project teams showcase prototypes and recruiters look for innovative ideas, especially relevant for engineering and CS students.
archival_memory.hackathon_experience: Remembered the second-year hackathon with thousands of students from various backgrounds participating for 24-36 hours. Beginners learned GitHub basics while advanced teams used machine learning for real-time image recognition. Sponsors and mentors provided help. Formed a team with casual acquaintances; the shared experience of eating stale pizza at 3 a.m., debugging code, and cheering each other on created strong, lasting bonds—highlighting the unique friendships formed through shared challenges and collaborative efforts.
archival_memory.dorm_life_engi_house: Stayed in 'The Engi-House,' a dorm specifically for engineering majors. Legendary late-night coding sessions in the common lounge with students working on Data Structures assignments, streaming e-sports, and occasionally stressed out due to energy drinks. A supportive environment where peers offered quick help when stuck. Held potlucks, watched Netflix, and hosted small talent shows to unwind and build camaraderie beyond academics.
archival_memory.volunteering_tech_for_good: Volunteers at 'Tech for Good' outreach events, helping local high school students learn programming and problem-solving through mini-workshops on web development and basic Python. Rewarding to see younger students excited when they create simple games or animated webpages. Reflects on personal journey as a beginner in tech, emphasizing the importance of providing positive first experiences and inspiring the next generation in STEM fields.
archival_memory.campus_social_scene: Lively social scene with Greek life, though the user never joined a fraternity. Found strong connections through specialized clubs: a friend joined the Robotics Team and now shares a close bond with teammates, forming a 'second family' for weekend hangouts, movie nights, and dinners. The user has grown closer to members of the VR/AR Club and CS Society, spending time joking, complaining about cafeteria food, and planning weekend hikes together—highlighting meaningful, interest-based friendships beyond academic or professional settings.
archival_memory.senior_week_campus_tradition: Senior Week is a series of events leading up to graduation, including a formal dance, a carnival, and a photo day in caps and gowns at iconic campus landmarks. Described as bittersweet—filled with laughter, nostalgia, and a sense of finality as students prepare to leave. Former seniors recall it as one of the best weeks of their college lives. The user is both excited and anxious, reflecting on four years of memories and the transition out of student life.
archival_memory.rivalry_game_campus_tradition: Annual Rivalry Game where sports teams face off against a major rival college across various sports. Despite not being a dedicated sports fan, the user loves the electric campus energy—people dress in school colors, paint faces, and carry banners. A massive pep rally with fireworks the night before the football game brings the community together. Friends gather in dorms or local bars to watch and cheer. Celebrations last all weekend if victorious, and even in losses, the community commiserates. A unifying tradition that brings together students from all majors, including business, art, and engineering.
archival_memory.e_sports_official_recognition: School’s e-sports team has gained official recognition, with a dedicated arena for tournaments. Students gather in large numbers to cheer on teams during League of Legends or Overwatch matches, often filling the seating area and watching live streams. Highlights a broader definition of campus sports and community, showing how e-sports have evolved into a legitimate and vibrant part of campus culture, a shift from traditional views that limited 'sports' to basketball or football.
archival_memory.midnight_breakfast_finals_week: Annual 'Midnight Breakfast' during finals week where stressed students gather at midnight in the dining hall for pancakes and cereal. Professors serve food, and the school band sometimes performs. A morale-boosting tradition that fosters camaraderie and reminds students they’re not alone in their exam anxiety. Highlights the campus’s effort to balance academic pressure with fun and community, making it a meaningful part of campus culture.
archival_memory.overall_campus_life_reflection: Campus life is what you make of it—enriched by exploring new communities, connecting with people, and joining clubs. Despite the demanding workload in Computer Science, participation in events, volunteering, and social activities has been highly rewarding. Will remember late-night coding, silly dorm game nights, Tech Fest presentations, hackathon adrenaline, and the excitement of the Rivalry Game. Describes it as a whirlwind but emphasizes that the experience is invaluable and would not be traded. Offers to show others favorite spots and introduce them to clubs, highlighting that there’s something for everyone and expressing genuine gratitude for embracing all campus offerings.
archival_memory.future_plans: Leaning towards a 5-year industry career, with grad school as a potential future option.
archival_memory.job_market_aim: Interested in software engineering roles in data visualization, VR/AR, and data-driven products. Passionate about interactive datasets and open-source tools. Targeting startups in VR for healthcare/engineering, not just big tech.
archival_memory.search_process: In campus recruiting; applied for software/data engineering roles. Summer internship at logistics data analytics startup: built UIs and real-time data pipelines. Gained hands-on development experience and confidence.
archival_memory.grad_school_interest: Interested in continuing research in immersive analytics or HCI for large datasets. Enjoys deep exploration through workshop papers and conference submissions. Considering a master's part-time while working or a full PhD, weighing practical application vs. specialized R&D opportunities.
archival_memory.professional_environment_preference: Thrives on teamwork and problem-solving in high-stakes scenarios. Prefers cross-functional collaboration with designers, data scientists, product managers, and domain experts. Enjoys iterative prototyping and interdisciplinary environments, similar to research lab experience.
archival_memory.financial_considerations: Concerned about student loans; prefers stable industry income for financial stability and debt reduction. Grad school funding is uncertain—stipends vary, tuition is common, scholarships are competitive.
archival_memory.timeline_and_interview_preparation: On top of hiring deadlines. Weekly interview prep: coding problems, data structures, algorithms. Advanced courses(Advanced Algorithms, Distributed Systems) build confidence in system design and technical interviews.
archival_memory.recruiter_interactions: Received LinkedIn outreach from companies. Aware hiring process is ongoing. Exploring local startups for hands-on roles. Inspired by joining a new VR startup and building products from scratch.
archival_memory.entrepreneurship_idea: Considering a VR training simulator or interactive data platform post-industry experience. Want to team with classmates or lab members. Aware of startup risks. Parents support but stress financial independence and practicality.
archival_memory.location_considerations: Considering relocation for job opportunities in tech hubs(Silicon Valley, Seattle, Austin, Midwest). Not opposed to moving, but concerned about visitation logistics with family. Open to remote or hybrid roles to live near family or in a comfortable location.
archival_memory.growth_mindset: Committed to lifelong learning and growth. Aim to specialize in immersive tech for data. Stay curious, avoid stagnation. Next steps: finish senior year, continue interviewing, decide by late spring. Confident in flexibility and adaptability.
archival_memory.small_getaways_campus_weekends: Smaller getaways with roommates on weekends. Drive to state parks or nearby beach towns. Pack snacks, fishing rods, turn up music. Set up camp or rent cabins. Once in a remote area with no cellphone reception—initially frustrating, but ended up being a digital detox. Hiked, told stories, enjoyed nature. Realized it recharged me for programming tasks back at campus.
